speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for Health (a) what is the Ministry doing to reduce the waiting time for dental treatment at polyclinics; (b) whether appointments for diagnosis and treatment can be made together with closer intervals; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider getting private practitioners onboard to relieve the manpower shortage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to expand capacity to address the increasing demand for dental services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This includes building more dental facilities in the upcoming new polyclinics, such as Punggol Polyclinic, as well as expanding existing polyclinic dental facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Polyclinics also inform patients about availability of CHAS dental clinics, where eligible patients can also access primary dental care if they choose to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Patients assessed to require immediate treatment can be attended to immediately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Most dental conditions are diagnosed and treated at the same sitting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, a minority of patients require additional appointments for more extensive treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In such cases, when the next appointment is scheduled will depend on the urgency of the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to monitor and meet the primary dental care needs of Singaporeans through both our polyclinics and CHAS dental clinics.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was told by my residents that National Dental Centre Singapore is very shorthanded and the waiting time can be more than a year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think a year is a little bit too long, and this is very concerning for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is: can residents seek treatment at the existing dental clinics, for example, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital and Changi Hospital?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Or are they now designated as private dental clinics?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Third question: do the dental clinic at polyclinics provide specialised dental treatment, such as root canal treatment?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Only dental conditions that require specialist dental care will be referred for management at the national specialty centres.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The new National Dental Centre Singapore will be expanded as part of the overall Outram campus plan which will be redeveloped in phases.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, the National University Hospital (NUH) Dental Centre has also started accepting specialty referrals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, not only just the National Dental Centre, the NUH Dental Centre does accept specialty referrals as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Er Dr Lee also mentioned about whether such subsidised cases can be provided at the other hospitals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The reason for this is that it allows consolidation of manpower as well as specialty resources for the provision of these specialty services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we also provide training opportunities for dental students as well as specialist training.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I have a resident who has been receiving treatment at Ng Teng Fong General Hospital but then, lately, he was told that he cannot go there anymore because now it is designated as a private dental clinic.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, all dental services in other hospitals other than what I have described are to provide private dental specialty services to patients.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have mentioned the reasons: to consolidate manpower resources at the three designated centres and, at the same time, provide opportunities for training of our dental specialists.
